title: Temporal Dead Zone (TDZ)
description: let and const bindings exist from block-entry but throw ReferenceError until their declaration line is reached — unlike var, which hoists with the value undefined.

notes: TDZ is per-binding-per-scope: the dead zone runs from block-entry to the declaration line, then the binding becomes live.
`typeof` throws inside the TDZ — the one place where typeof on a name is unsafe. On a truly undeclared name, typeof still returns "undefined".
`const` has the same TDZ behavior as `let` (plus immutability). Only `var` skips the TDZ — it hoists with the value `undefined`.
TDZ errors are always `ReferenceError`, never `SyntaxError` (the binding is valid; the access is just too early).
Restructure to fix: declare the let/const FIRST in the block, or move the read AFTER the declaration line.

questions.explain: var hoists with the value `undefined` — no TDZ, just a hoisted-but-not-yet-assigned binding.

questions.q: What happens when `console.log(b); let b = 1;` runs?
questions.explain: let bindings exist from block-entry but are in the Temporal Dead Zone until the declaration line — reading them throws ReferenceError.

questions.q: Which of these throws? `(A) console.log(typeof notDeclaredAnywhere)`  `(B) { console.log(typeof x); let x; }`
questions.explain: typeof on a truly undeclared name returns "undefined" safely. But typeof on a let/const inside its TDZ DOES throw — the binding exists, it's just not initialized yet.

L3.prompt: Write `inTdz(fn)` that calls fn and returns the error name if it throws, otherwise the string "ok". Use it to prove all three TDZ cases throw ReferenceError: reading a `let`, `typeof` on a `let`, and reading a `const` — each before its declaration. Log the three results, one per line.
hints: The arrow body is its own block scope — `let a = 1` inside it creates a TDZ for `a` from the block-entry to that line.
All three reads happen BEFORE the declaration line, so the inner console.log never fires — the read itself throws.
`typeof` is normally the safe way to probe an identifier, but inside a TDZ it throws like any other read.
